title: Abyss: Depths, Crafting and the Vessel of Kulemak
summary: How Abyss works in Path of Exile 2 from the map fissure through the Abyssal Depths, Abyss crafting and rewards, Atlas points, the Unique boss invitation and the Vessel of Kulemak gate.
description: A reference for the Abyss end-game system in Path of Exile 2: finding Abyss on the Atlas, following the fissure, the Depths, Abyss crafting and rewards, Atlas points, the Unique boss invitation and the Vessel of Kulemak path.
prerequisites: Maps unlocked and you can sustain Waystones
A character fast enough to follow the fissure
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: The Vessel of Kulemak, the Abyss pinnacle boss of Path of Exile 2

items.title: What is an Abyss on the Atlas?
body: An Abyss shows up as a fissure or crack on the map. Following it opens nodes along a line, and reaching the end can open the Abyssal Depths.
The line keeps moving, so a fast character follows more of it and reaches the Depths more often.

items.title: How do I enter the Depths?
body: The Abyssal Depths open when you clear enough of the fissure line. A bigger, faster clear raises the chance the Depths appear.

items.title: What is the Unique boss invitation for?
body: The Unique boss drops an invitation. That invitation is the gate to the Vessel of Kulemak, the Abyss pinnacle boss.

items.title: What does Abyss crafting give?
body: Abyss rewards feed crafting: jewels, socketables and special items such as The Master's Reach come from Abyss content.

sections.title: Finding Abyss on the Atlas
paragraphs: Abyss appears as a fissure node on the Atlas. Running a map that contains it spawns the crack in the zone.
The fissure draws a line across the map as you fight along it. Killing monsters near the line extends it; ignoring it lets it close.
Faster, more mobile characters follow the line further, which is why move speed and clear speed matter more for Abyss than for static encounters.
bullets: Line extends as you kill along it
Speed matters more than raw damage

sections.title: Abyss path diagnostic
sections.intro: Pick the symptom you hit and follow the fix.

rules.title: Fissure closed before you finished
steps: You fell behind the moving line; the fissure closes if you stop killing along it.
Use a faster, more mobile character or clear the path ahead before the line arrives.
Re-run the Abyss map; the line is random each time.

rules.title: Abyssal Depths did not appear
steps: The Depths open only after enough of the line is cleared; a short clear will not trigger them.
Push further along the line and kill the packs it spawns.
Confirm the map actually had an Abyss node before blaming the spawn.

rules.title: Invitation cannot be used
steps: The invitation comes from the Unique boss, not a normal fissure; a normal run will not drop it.
Clear the Abyss Unique boss first, then use the invitation where the boss page directs.
Check you meet any gate the invitation requires before using it.

defaultResult.title: Path looks normal
steps: If none of the above match, the Abyss ran as expected; follow the line to the Depths and the Unique boss.

sections.title: Encounter stages
paragraphs: Stage one is the fissure line: follow it, kill the spawns, and extend it as far as you can.
Stage two is the Abyssal Depths if it opens: a bonus area with chests and the Abyss boss fight.
Stage three is the Unique boss, which is what drops the invitation that gates the pinnacle.

sections.title: Abyssal Depths
paragraphs: The Abyssal Depths are the bonus space opened by a strong fissure clear. They hold richer chests than the surface line.
The Depths are where the Abyss boss appears, so treating them as the real payoff of the encounter is correct.
Note the 0.5.4 fix: Atlas Passives that did not apply inside the Depths before now work, so old reward math from pre-0.5.4 Depths is stale.
bullets: Bonus space from a strong clear

sections.title: Rewards and crafting
paragraphs: Abyss rewards split into currencies, jewels, socketables and special items. The Master's Reach is one of the notable special drops.
Socketables from Abyss feed your gear; jewels from the Depths are the higher-value crafting target.
Decide what you farm before the run: if you want The Master's Reach, push Depths and the Unique boss rather than skimming the surface line.
bullets: The Master's Reach is a notable drop

sections.title: Reaching the Vessel of Kulemak
paragraphs: The Vessel of Kulemak is the Abyss pinnacle boss, reached through the Unique boss invitation chain.
It assumes a character that already clears Abyssal Depths and the Unique boss, so do not attempt it under-geared.
This guide covers the path and preparation; the boss page covers the Vessel of Kulemak's attacks in detail once reachable.

sections.intro: Community experiences; treat as strategy, not guaranteed math.

cards.title: Speed wins Abyss
body: Players consistently report that move speed and clear speed decide whether the Depths open at all.

cards.title: Depths are the payoff
body: Most valuable Abyss loot comes from the Depths and the Unique boss, not the surface line.

cards.title: Invitation from the Unique only
body: Normal fissure runs never drop the invitation; only the Unique boss does.

sections.title: Common problems
paragraphs: If the fissure keeps closing, you are too slow; switch to a faster, more mobile character or pre-clear the path.
If the Depths never open, your clear is too short; follow the line further and kill its packs.
If the invitation never drops, you are running normal fissures; only the Unique boss drops it.
